## Purpose

`backend/agents` is the execution kernel. It compiles declarative `workflow.yaml` manifests
into a typed `CompiledWorkflow`/`Step` DAG, drives that DAG deterministically through a
`CapabilityRegistry` of self-registering strategies/gates/validators/deliverables/tools/hooks,
and adapts each step's LLM call onto a LangChain `deepagents` graph.

**It knows no workflow by name** — every workflow-specific behaviour is a declared capability
reference resolved at compile time, never an `if pipeline_type == ...` branch in the kernel.
`backend/app/agents/` (the FastAPI layer), `backend/app/api/`, and the WebSocket run driver all
sit on top of this module; it is the single most important module in the repo.

## Shape

Major sub-areas, from manifest to execution:

- `workflows/` — the compiler pipeline. [manifest.py](../../backend/agents/workflows/manifest.py) (`load_manifest`) parses
  `agents/workflows/<id>/workflow.yaml` via `yaml.safe_load` with strict top-level key
  allow-listing (no `when:`/`if:`/`${...}` — control flow has nowhere to live, keeping
  manifests pure data). [compiler.py](../../backend/agents/workflows/compiler.py) (`WorkflowCompiler`) resolves every declared capability
  name against the `CapabilityRegistry` (unknown name -> `CompilerError` naming the bad
  reference) and turns raw step dicts into typed `Step`s with a cycle-free DAG check.
  [plan.py](../../backend/agents/workflows/plan.py) defines the typed output (`CompiledWorkflow`, `Step`, `DeliverableSpec`,
  `ClarifySpec`, `FanoutSpec`, `ToolPermissions`, …). [selections.py](../../backend/agents/workflows/selections.py) handles per-run
  capability selection/overrides.

- `capabilities/` — the self-registering registry (`registry.py`). A module-level
  `@register(kind, name, user_allowed=...)` decorator binds `(kind, name) -> impl` at import;
  `_KNOWN` is a pure membership set the compiler validates against with zero impls bound.
  `discover()` lazily imports every impl subpackage (never at compiler-import time) so the
  compiler's INV-4 membership check stays impl-free. `base.py` defines the Protocol ports the
  kernel depends on exclusively (hexagonal ports-and-adapters): `ExecutionStrategy`,
  `Validator`, `GateHandler`, `DeliverableResolver`, `ContextProvider`, `PostStep`,
  `PromptAssemblyPolicy`, `AgentRuntimeAdapter`, `ToolProvider`, `SkillProvider`,
  `HookHandler`, `IntegrationProvider`.

  Concrete impls live in subpackages named after their kind: `strategies/` (`single_shot`,
  `task_loop`, `fanout_batch`, `wave_scheduler`), `gates/` (`human`, `validation`, `approval`,
  `security`), `validators/` (structural checks plus exec-backed
  `code_compile`/`code_test`/`code_lint`), `deliverables/` (`single_file`,
  `serialized_sandbox`, `streamed_text`, `ppt`, `repo_diff`), `merge/` (`copy_disjoint`,
  `git_3way`, `json_merge`, `html_fragment` — fan-out result merging), `context_providers/`
  (`opendesign`, `previous_run`, `repo`, `uploaded_files`, `conversation`), `hooks/`
  (`behavioral`, `secret_scan`, `otel_tracing`, `audit_logger`), plus `tools/`, `skills/`,
  `runtimes/` (`langchain_deepagents`), `prompt/`, `mcp_servers/`, `integration_providers/`,
  `task_parsers/`, `compaction/`, `post_steps/`. [model_catalog.py](../../backend/agents/capabilities/model_catalog.py)/[model_pricing.py](../../backend/agents/capabilities/model_pricing.py) hold
  model metadata and cost estimation as name-only data capabilities.

- `execution_engine/` — the kernel proper. [engine.py](../../backend/agents/execution_engine/engine.py) (`ExecutionEngine`) is the single entry
  point (`execute()`) that validates the DAG via [resolver.py](../../backend/agents/execution_engine/resolver.py)'s `WorkflowResolver`, runs an
  optional Deep-Planner gate, drives domain agents in topological order, evaluates
  Human/Validation gates, and emits the WebSocket event envelope. [context.py](../../backend/agents/execution_engine/context.py)
  (`ExecutionContext`) is the per-run state threaded through every step. [state_machine.py](../../backend/agents/execution_engine/state_machine.py)
  (`get_state_machine`) tracks run status transitions. [budget.py](../../backend/agents/execution_engine/budget.py) enforces token/cost ceilings
  (`BudgetManager`, `BudgetExceeded`). [clarify_engine.py](../../backend/agents/execution_engine/clarify_engine.py) drives the CLARIFY_REQUIRED
  human-in-the-loop loop. [fanout.py](../../backend/agents/execution_engine/fanout.py) implements parallel sub-agent fan-out with isolation
  scopes (`shared_read` / `sub_sandbox` / `worktree`). [kernel_services.py](../../backend/agents/execution_engine/kernel_services.py),
  [ndjson_adapter.py](../../backend/agents/execution_engine/ndjson_adapter.py), [resolver.py](../../backend/agents/execution_engine/resolver.py), and [od_context.py](../../backend/agents/execution_engine/od_context.py) are supporting services for prompt
  streaming, workflow-DAG validation, and OpenDesign template/craft context.

- [runtime/base.py](../../backend/agents/runtime/base.py) — a second port layer, distinct from [capabilities/base.py](../../backend/agents/capabilities/base.py): the
  `RuntimeEnvironment`/`Workspace`/`ExecutionPolicy`/`IsolationProvider` Protocols that
  abstract workspace provisioning (the "ECS-swap seam" — a later remote-backed runtime can
  implement `RuntimeEnvironment.create_workspace()` with zero kernel change). The only bound
  impl today is [app/agents/runtime/local.py](../../backend/app/agents/runtime/local.py)'s `LocalSandboxRuntime`.

- Agent identity layer — [loader.py](../../backend/agents/loader.py) (`load_agent_spec`, `AgentSpec`) reads and validates
  `agents/prompts/<id>/AGENT.md` frontmatter (one file per agent, ~80+ agents). `registry.py`
  holds `PIPELINE_AGENTS` (the ordered agent-ID membership per pipeline — the single source of
  truth the compiled manifest is asserted against at run entry) plus `get_pipeline_agents()`,
  `get_agent_by_id()`, `get_all_agents_flat()`, and `allowed_custom_agent_ids()` (the
  run_pipeline request allow-list, branch-derived from `*_revision` suffixes rather than a
  hand-maintained list). [factory.py](../../backend/agents/factory.py) (`create_runner`, `AgentContext`) composes the final
  system prompt in a fixed block order (`injects -> guardrails -> skills -> hooks ->
  constitution -> prompt body`) and resolves the agent's tool set, then instantiates a
  `DeepAgentRunner`. [model_policy.py](../../backend/agents/model_policy.py) (`ModelResolver`) picks the model per agent/run.

- `planner/` — [smart_planner.py](../../backend/agents/planner/smart_planner.py) (`SmartPlanner`) is a single structured LLM call (not a
  ReAct tool loop) that turns a user brief + pipeline type into a `PlanningContext` JSON
  (missing-information detection, inferred constraints/personas/NFRs, quality targets) using a
  built-in per-pipeline `DOMAIN_KB`. [tools.py](../../backend/agents/planner/tools.py) holds stub `PLANNING_TOOLS` for the
  `"planning"` tool set.

- Other top-level pieces: [artifact_store/store.py](../../backend/agents/artifact_store/store.py) plus [artifacts/graph.py](../../backend/agents/artifacts/graph.py)
  (`ArtifactGraph`) persist and retrieve typed inter-agent artifacts; [authz.py](../../backend/agents/authz.py)
  (`ScopedStore`) enforces per-owner data scoping; [workflow_memory/memory.py](../../backend/agents/workflow_memory/memory.py) holds the
  per-user "Constitution" (durable cross-run preferences) injected into prompts.

## Why this shape

The core design bet is **capability-registry indirection over a workflow-name switch**: the
compiler and registry enforce (via the `_KNOWN` membership set and `is_registered`) that a
manifest can only reference *declared* capabilities, and the engine resolves them by
`(kind, name)` — so the kernel package never contains a literal pipeline ID or workflow name
(SC-001/INV-1 in the code's own terms). Adding a capability is "add a module + `@register`
decorator," not "add a branch to the engine."

This is why `discover()` is lazy and separate from the compiler's `_KNOWN` check: the compiler
must be able to validate manifest references with zero heavy implementations imported, so
compile-time validation and runtime dispatch are deliberately split into two data structures
(`_KNOWN` vs `_IMPLS`).

Two distinct port layers exist on purpose. [capabilities/base.py](../../backend/agents/capabilities/base.py) abstracts *what a step does*
(strategy/validator/gate/deliverable/...), while [runtime/base.py](../../backend/agents/runtime/base.py) abstracts *where it runs*
(workspace provisioning/isolation). Conflating them would couple the capability system to a
specific execution substrate; keeping them separate is what lets a future remote/ECS-backed
`RuntimeEnvironment` swap in without touching a single capability impl.

The registry deliberately keeps two parallel "membership" structures that must stay in
lock-step: `agents/registry.py::PIPELINE_AGENTS` (which agents belong to a pipeline, and in
what order) and each pipeline's `workflow.yaml` (how each step runs). **The engine asserts
these agree at run entry and raises `RuntimeError` on drift** rather than silently picking one
— the manifest and the registry are two independently-edited sources of truth, and this is the
seam that catches them diverging.

`context_from` in `AGENT.md` is deliberately marked legacy/vestigial in the code comments: it
is still parsed for backward compatibility, but live inter-agent context routing goes through
the typed `produces`/`consumes` contracts instead, because that is what participates in the
compiler's DAG validation (`WorkflowResolver`) — a free-text `context_from` reference can't be
statically checked the way a typed produces/consumes edge can.

Exec-capable capabilities (`code_compile`/`code_test`/`code_lint`, `exec_command` on
`Workspace`) are kept off the user-grantable palette by default (`user_allowed=False` in
`_TRUST`) and only ever reach a subprocess through the `ctx.runner`/workspace handle — never a
direct subprocess call from inside a capability module — so the trust boundary is enforced at
one seam instead of scattered across every capability that might want to shell out.
